utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon -- good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Today we'll have a housekeeping session but I'll first invite Madam Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T, The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The accused are not present. Chamber was informed that both accused have waived their right to be present today and that's not new for housekeeping sessions. Mr. Jordash, Mr. Petrovic, that is correct, I take it? I haven't seen yet the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, next time if the accused waived their right to be present, the Chamber advises you not only to inform the Chamber but also the Registry because otherwise transport police is waiting and there's all kind of confusion. I do understand that Chamber has been informed, but the Registry not, which caused quite a bit of fuss this morning, so if you would please keep that in mind for future occasions. Then I have quite a number of items on my agenda. We'll start with the items which were found already in the Scheduling Order, and I start with what the Registry was supposed to prepare. Madam Registrar, has an English translation been attached to Exhibit P1287?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been attached in e-court; therefore it now is part of it. Then has the English translation of Exhibit P767, which was an erroneous translation, has it been replaced with document ID 0202-7320?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then have English translations been attached to the documents with Exhibit numbers D280 up to and including D290?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has document ID 1D06-4194 been attached to document D266?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next one needs a bit more attention. The Chamber has instructed the Registry to attach document 1D04-6949 to document D274, but this -- under this document identification number we also find a B/C/S attachment, whereas it was only intended that an English translation should be attached to D274. Therefore, the Stanisic Defence is invited to detach the English translation -- the B/C/S attachment so that only the English translation remains and that then should be attached to D274. Is this clear? Madam Registrar, any questions in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then has 1D05-6514 been attached to document D310?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Then I go through instructions given to the parties. First, Prosecution, has a surrogate sheet been uploaded for Exhibit P2977?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, it has, Your Honour, um, it's been uploaded with doc ID V000-7024.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, that should then be attached to surrogate sheet too, or does it get a separate number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It can be attached [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it should be then attached to P2977. Ms. Marcus, has a B/C/S version of Exhibit P243 [Realtime transcript read in error "P2493"] been uploaded which corresponds to the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's uploaded under doc ID 0209-4822.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, if something is uploaded, I take it that if it's mentioned here, that you can attach whatever is uploaded to the original document and if there are any problems, I'd like you to raise your voice, and in the absence of any comments, we'll just move on. Ms. Marcus, has a revised English translation been up loaded of Exhibit P813 which includes the translation of the pages 4 to 8 of the original document?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It is uploaded under doc ID X019-6203-EDT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then next on the agenda: Has a revised document Exhibit P1050 corresponding to its English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, it has. It's uploaded as doc ID 0608-0177-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Marcus, have revised English translations of Exhibit P1040, P1041 and P1042 been uploaded corresponding in scope to the original documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For Exhibit P1040, we have uploaded doc ID 0263-3400-EDT. For Exhibit P1041 we have 0263-3404-EDT. And for Exhibit P1042 we have 0216-2249-EDT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then moving to the next one, has a B/C/S translation been uploaded of Exhibits P1043 and an English translation of Exhibit P1011.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to these documents, they are the constitution, the SFRY constitution. The difference between the English and the B/C/S was that there were extra sections included but the actual articles were corresponding, the English and the B/C/S. So what we've done is we've undertaken to ask the language assistants to compare the two documents and we -- what we've done is we have made them corresponds according to -- just to the articles of the constitutions. So those corresponding versions, which I think Your Honours will find now match each other, the English to the B/C/S, we have uploaded those two versions as 65 ter 2868.1 and 65 ter 715.1 respectively. So we would propose, with Your Honours' leave, that those 65 ter numbers be uploaded one as P1011 and one as P1043. They now correspond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, is this workable for you?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have -- we have new content for Exhibit P1011 and P1043, although not that much different from what it earlier was. Has a revised English translation been uploaded of Exhibit P839 which includes translation of the pages 13 to 16 of the original, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have two doc IDs for this. One is X019-6320-BCST and X019-6329.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is one for the B/C/S and one for the English translation? What makes it two documents now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just one moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, apparently the original document has some B/C/S and some English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So the B/C/S is the translation of English and vice-versa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, is that clear enough for you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Next one: Has a correct English translation been uploaded of Exhibit P732.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's uploaded at doc ID 0218-6591-EDT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has a revised B/C/S version of Exhibit P853 been uploaded in which extraneous -- the extraneous page 3 has been eliminated?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's uploaded as doc ID 0109-8852.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then has the Prosecution verified whether P1287 is a duplicate of P2482, and what is the result?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've compared the two documents. They are the same original text but one of the documents has a lot of additional markings on it which, for us, are relevant. Therefore, our proposal -- so the difference is P1287 is from the Croatian state archives, and it contains the stamp of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, whereas P2484 is from the ABiH archives, does not contain the stamp but has handwriting which includes Roman numeral II and what we submit are the initials of Franko Simatovic. Therefore, the stamps and notations at the end of these documents are different. We uploaded the same translation for both, which was incorrect because P2484 with the stamp not appearing, it does appear in the translation. So we would submit that there should be two separate documents and we will undertake to provide a revised translation for P2484. We have submitted it already and we anticipate that it should be ready sometime this morning. I'll keep Your Honours informed of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so the two documents remain known under their individual numbers and a new translation is being prepared for P2484.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, P2484 was already admitted into evidence, let me just check. Yes, I think it was. It doesn't appear on the MFI list.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, it should be marked that a new translation is being prepared at this moment and should then replace the translation which was attached to it until now. Has an English translation been uploaded of Exhibit P3000?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has been uploaded as doc ID 0600-7963-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that exhibit now is complete with this translation. Has a complete English translation been uploaded of Exhibit P1812?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. It has been uploaded with doc ID Y001-2185-EDT.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Same question for P878?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: It has doc ID 0104-7916-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Marcus. Then the next question is whether the Prosecution is of the view that Exhibits D390 up to and including D392 and D395 can be public exhibits, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we suggest that they remain under seal. We did not tender the documents so we did not notify Serbia that they may be used, therefore the Serbian authorities have not had an opportunity to seek protective measures. So we suggest until the Stanisic Defence can notify Serbia and Serbia has this opportunity, that the documents remain under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When will we hear from you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, we'll do that straightaway and we are in Serbia's hands in relation to their response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you need the assistance of the Chamber, please don't hesitate to ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next question of my list on this Scheduling Order is that the Prosecution is invited to advise the Chamber whether its comments about the status of parts of Witness Bosnic's testimony are to be understood as a request to lift the confidentiality of these parts, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we so request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any objection against granting the request, confidentiality to be lifted of part of the testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber will decide most likely this morning about the status of those parts of the testimony. Ms. Marcus, the next number invites you to advise the Chamber whether the Prosecution intends to recall witnesses Novakovic, Corbic or Lekovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to these witnesses, we still have several outstanding RFAs to Serbia and to a number of different agencies. We would appreciate the opportunity to wait until we receive and process those responses to make a final decision as to the recall of these witness. We are doing our utmost to expedite that process to the extent it's within our ability do so and we'll keep the Chamber informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which also means that witnesses Novakovic and Corbic are still under a -- they are still barred from communicating with whomever about their testimony, that remains in place. Yes, number 17 as far as the Prosecution is concerned in the scheduling, we'll come back to that later. It was about the bar table motion. We'll revisit that matter soon. Then I move to the Stanisic Defence, the questions outstanding. Mr. Jordash, D451 needs to remain under seal or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then unless there's any objection, and apparently there's not, D451 is now a public document. Mr. Jordash, has a revised English translation been uploaded of Exhibit D205?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it has. Yes, it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, again unless there are any problems, revised or newly uploaded translations or documents at the specific request of the Chamber of course can replace then the original -- originally uploaded documents. If there's any question at any point in time, I would like to hear from you. Next one, Mr. Jordash, has a revised English translation been uploaded of D305?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it has, at 65 ter 1D02395.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the previous one, you didn't give an ID number and since that has been done consequently by the Prosecution, that was about D205, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's been uploaded under doc ID -- sorry under doc ID 0608-4196. By the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that D205?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then that doc ID is now on the record as well. I move on, has a complete English translation been uploaded of document D380?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, we are still waiting a full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the Stanisic Defence update the other parties and the Chamber on its investigations about the provenance of document D56, a document which was earlier not admitted but was re-tendered by the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We obtained it from Mr. Stanisic. We've approached the National Council but we haven't received any responses yet as to whether they've -- have the document in their possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can anything more be said about from whom Mr. Stanisic received it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, not at the moment. I can and should have asked Mr. Stanisic further about that, and didn't. I can ask him about it and inform the Chamber at the next court hearing. I beg your pardon, sorry, there is more information. It was from one of Mr. Stanisic's assistants which is a Risto Vejovic [phoen] who is dead. He died, I think, over the last few years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there -- but we have no further information on where Mr. Vejovic got it, or you say it's one of his assistants. Any particular time-frame for assisting Mr. Stanisic or specific position? Was he -- I mean, this is a name, it may well be that in the evidence more is known about him, but I don't have that on the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, neither do I, but I do know he provided statements to the Prosecution and so further information can be obtained readily and I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could then perhaps the Stanisic Defence and the Prosecution sit together and see what information they have about the source of these documents, it may well be he said something about it in the statement he has given, so that we get the best information available at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to you whether it will be tea or coffee, Ms. Marcus, Mr. Jordash. The next item is about Exhibit P179 and Exhibit P473. I think the Prosecution has expressed that there is agreement about signatures of page 2 of the B/C/S version of Exhibit P179 and page 1 of the B/C/S version of Exhibit P473. I would just like to know whether the Stanisic confirms this agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do. That's hereby on the record. Now, I, as I said before, I come back to the bar table submission. You were invited, Mr. Jordash, to file not later than six days before the housekeeping session an update on the -- your first bar table submission, which was filed on the 3rd of February, 2011, and more specifically, whether you still intended to bar table this document as opposed to tendering them through witnesses. Now, we have been informed that there was an informal communication that the Stanisic Defence would file a broader bar table motion which would include documents from this initial bar table motion. The question then immediately arises when do you intend to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just take a moment, please, and just consult with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We'll be in a position to file the bar table motion at some point next week. The problem, however, will still remain that some of these documents have redactions. We are hoping to visit the relevant archives in the next two weeks, so it may be that while we are in a position to file the bar table next week, it may not be the most efficient use of resources to do that before we've been to Belgrade and seen the relevant documents without redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I tend to agree with you that it doesn't make much sense to hasten now to file a motion which has to be amended within ten days from it being filed. Now at the same time of course bar table motions should be filed preferably before the judgement has been delivered, isn't it? Don't forgive -- forgive me my bad sense of humour in the early morning hours of this day, but what about - today, we are at the 24th of November - if the Stanisic Defence, I'm looking specifically at you, Ms. Marcus, would have filed its bar table motion by mid-December but then the final one, after having checked the non-redacted originals in Belgrade, would that be a good idea?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, generally speaking we are just a little bit concerned about the lack of closure of the Stanisic Defence case and the timing of that, so I just wanted to put that concern on the record. But it seems to me that since we are going to have at least two of their witnesses in December, anyway, that there wouldn't be any problem, I think, with that motion being filed at the time Your Honour specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, perhaps I take it that you worked on the preparation of such a motion anyhow, so where you have to verify the originals, the unredacted originals, perhaps you could already provide a list of the documents you intend to bar table to Ms. Marcus so that she can start working on it, knowing that there is uncertainty about some documents where you still have to inspect the original non-redacted versions. Is that a solution that you, for example, provide that by the end of next week to Ms. Marcus so that the Prosecution can proceed in its preparations?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. Just for Your Honours' information, we intend to file, I think, at least two bar table motions. The first one will relate specifically to state security reports and the like where obviously the issue of redactions is most relevant. So we can provide a list of those documents, I think, probably by the end of the week to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then the other one, do I have to understand that the other bar table motion that -- because we are not now talking about one broader one but about two bar table motions, is there any redaction issue involved there?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, the second and maybe even the third will relate to such things as supplies to Bosnia and supplies to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So when I earlier asked when do you intend to file the broader bar table motion, I now have to be more specific. The first one is clear, we agreed that it is -- that the redactions play a role there and that you provide Ms. Marcus with a list and the motion will be filed by mid-December so as to avoid that we have to do it twice. Now for -- I call them now bar table motion 2, when do you intend to file that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If we could have until the same time and if there's a problem, we'll file for an extension. What we are trying to do is cut down a number of exhibits which is taking some time, so we are doing our best with the resources we have, but we would hope to file that by the middle of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that bar table motion 2 would contain what kind of material?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Bar table 2 will be almost exclusively concerning supplies to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then bar table motion number 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Everything remaining, such as supplies to the Krajina and then perhaps more miscellaneous, if I can put it like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leftovers. And what is your suggestion for the timing of bar table motion 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, we would hope again to do that by middle of December and that may be unrealistic but we are as keen as the Prosecution to get this done and close as much as we can, or finish as much as we can of our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Trying to be as understanding as we can, I think the delay to mid-December was due to the redactions. Frankly, I'm not so sure why the delay to mid-December for the other two. It would be our preference to have those two have an earlier dead-line than that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's simply not possible. With the resources we have, it's simply absolutely impossible. We have moved almost all our resources to dealing with these bar table motions and we are also having to deal with Milovanovic who is a big witness and the outstanding witnesses in our case, one of whom is also a rather large witness who testified in, I think, four or five trials before this Tribunal. So with the best will in the world with the resources we have, it's simply not possible. I should -- sorry. I should say that we have a team of two counsel, three legal assistants, and interns of I think at the moment five and everybody is working extremely hard. I just cannot see how we could do it earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll not revisit the earlier discussions about financing of the Stanisic Defence team. Let me -- Ms. Marcus, I do understand that you -- again, it was perhaps bad humour but you really would like to have the bar table motions before the judgement and for you, of course, it would be for further preparation. Now, what exactly would be lost for you if you would receive those let's say, by the 1st of January rather than the 1st of December? I mean, what would be the impact apart from, of course, the overall impact that the later it comes the less time you have to digest it and to comment on it, but how would it affect and impact on the proceedings in December?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is simply part of the overall concern about the lengthy delay in the ending the case and the sort of murky nature of their case still being open. That leaves a lot of uncertainty. The later we have the documents, the less opportunity we have to put it to the witnesses who are coming. We still don't know which witnesses are coming, but the -- the analysis of the documentation is something which -- which tells us more and more about their case. It's how they present their case and the later they present their case, the less opportunity that we have during the remainder of their case and the start of the Simatovic case to rebut those contentions. So generally speaking, it has to do with when their case closes and how we can prepare to respond to the documents that we receive, but I leave it in Your Honours' hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: None of that, respectfully, is an accurate portrayal of the situation. The Prosecution have the documents. They can use them and have been able to use them over the last few months during our case. They know what they are. They know the witnesses who are outstanding. I don't see what is lost and nothing my learned friend has just said indicates that anything is lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I think you, yourself, told us that you are trying to reduce the number of documents to find the most relevant ones, and, of course, all the time spent by the Prosecution on documents you at the end find not relevant enough to bar table them is, well, may be time which is wasted, lost, but we'll have a -- we'll consider the matter and we'll -- we'll see whether we give further instructions to you as to the timing of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the filing of the three, as I now understand, bar table motions. Then I move to the Simatovic Defence. The first question as found on page 4 of the Scheduling Order is moot by now or at least on hold. The second question was the date of the two proposed Simatovic Defence expert reports. I think you have indicated when you would file them, but we see that one of the reports is more than 700 pages and I think the Chamber has some concern about the size of the materials. I think there was also a matter of whether or not one of the witnesses were experts -- no, let's see, that's -- I leave that apart at this moment. We have a more than 700 pages report from one of your expert. Are there any related documents because we haven't seen the report, but we have had a look at the table of contents. Are there any problems with related documents and translation of related documents, especially if we end up in this size of reports that create sometimes additional problems? Could you update us on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as a Defence team we will do our best to avoid any problems. However, working with this report and the accompanying documents is not going to be easy at all. This report, 700 pages long, is supported by several hundreds of documents and some of those documents are being identified, are being compared with the documents which are on our 65 ter list, which are Prosecutor's documents, and those documents which are on none of the two and the report still refers to them. When we finish the process of identifying the documents and deciding which document falls under what category, the remainder of the document will be sent for translation. We expect that a significant number of documents is already on some of the lists belonging to a party to the proceedings, but they will be documents that were found on the EDS and that belong to other sources. The problem is huge, the workload is huge, but we are doing as fast as we can. We know, we are aware of the concern of our learned friends from the Prosecution with this regard. We'll try to deal with the questions that they put to us as soon as possible. However, as the Trial Chamber has remarked, the report is voluminous and refers to a significant number of documents. We are doing our best but we don't expect the job to be either easy or fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is the -- if you do not mind, Mr. Petrovic, this is the kind of observations like the winter will be cold and dark and snow may fall and we would then have to remove that snow from the roads. I mean, where is your work-plan? That's first of all. Where are we with the translation of the report itself? Have you provided the whole of the report to CLSS and have you any idea on when they would finish the translation of the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first an observation. I wish to be very honest before Trial Chamber and I would like to present the situation as it is, the situation may be somewhat darker but I can explain why, if you believe this may be necessary. As far as the translation of the documents is concerned, the report has been sent for translation at the beginning of August of this year. If I'm not mistaken, that was on the 4th of August to be very precise. According to the update we received a few days ago, the translation of the report will be finished by the end of this year. I'm talking about the report which is 700 pages long. Our second report, which is much more concise, will be translated by the end of the month of November. At least, that was what we heard from the translation service. We sent both reports in B/C/S versions to our colleagues from the OTP hoping that that would facilitate their preparation for the testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you explored with the OTP whether there are parts of the report where there's no dispute about? I mean, 700 pages is not nothing. That's -- having looked at the -- having looked at the table of contents, sometimes of the overall structure of armed forces or whatever, I wonder whether there are no areas where the parties have no dispute about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have still not put that question to my colleagues because I'm not sure whether they have succeeded to review everything in detail - I'm talking about the B/C/S material - but I believe that there are entire areas in both reports that may be uncontestable. That is my impression of the Prosecution's position. I believe that there are entire parts of those reports that the OTP will not contest at all but it's up to them to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether or not that's true, then you are choosing the wrong order, Mr. Petrovic. You shouldn't ask someone to write a report about matters which are not in dispute. If you say the overall structure - for example, I'm just giving one example - would most likely not be contested, then you sit together with the other party and say we want to establish the overall structures, we have an expert who could do so but if we agree on it then we just present that agreement to the Chamber. We don't have to hire a expensive expert to write a report about that, then to have it being translated which takes, that's August, September, October, November, December, that's five months. It's not that you start with a report and then later try to find out whether there's disagreement. You first should try to find out where the disagreement is, where the dispute is, and then to find an expert who will focus on that disagreement, rather than the other way around. I'm -- especially if it all results in 30 or 40 pages, fine, then perhaps it's easier to have that report written without, but if it results in 700 pages of report where you still are telling us that you now have to identify what underlying documents are still there to be translated, perhaps taking -- all that effort should be made only in respect of matters which are in dispute and not in relation to matters which are not disputed. That's the concern of the Chamber, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as regards the police expert, there may be some parts, but those parts could simply not be omitted from the text of the expert report because the expert report follows a logical line, it is a whole and some parts had to be included because we wanted to present a Trial Chamber with an expert report which is grounded, which has a basis, which has its inner logic and that inner logic is necessary for the work to appear to be integral. That's why some of the parts seem to be superfluous. There's not too many of them, but they had to be included to provide the report with a certain logic. As far as the military expert report is concerned I feel that it is necessary for me to say the following: Work with an expert who is a military expert and who is a joint expert of both teams, we started working with this expert many years before this Defence team was put in place. For a long time, it was believed that the person responsible for the expert report would be our colleagues from the Stanisic Defence team. At one point in time, and that point in time came, if I'm not mistaken, in May or June, decided to withdraw from our joint team effort so the expert report that had already been drafted and that the current Defence team could not influence at all, that expert report existed. There was no time, no resources to draft a new expert report. So we were actually put in a situation where we have very little choice. We needed the expert report. The expert report was drafted much before. It should have been our joint effort, our joint expert report, and as I said, one point in time it became only our expert report, although we did not have a decisive influence either on the structure of the report or the way it had been drafted. This creates additional problems. If my colleague Bakrac and I had been in charge from the very beginning I believe that things may have been different, however, this is the course that the events have taken so far. We are doing our utmost to remedy the situation but we are asking for your understanding with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm reluctant to intervene but my recollection is that that report was a joint effort from the beginning and we did withdraw from the report but our input into it was never intended to be the decisive one. It was a joint effort and I'm sorry to contradict Mr. Petrovic, but that report from the beginning, the funding of the report was joint, the direction to the expert was joint, and we decided not to pursue it. That's the situation from our perspective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apparently there are different views on what caused the present situation, I think it's not for the Chamber to explore that in depth. As a matter of fact, the Chamber is more interested at this moment in how the matter was resolved and whether you together, whether the Simatovic Defence alone -- my comments were of a totally different nature. They were why have you not sat together with the Prosecution to find out what really is in dispute so that the expert could focus on that? And now to say that the report was there already and, therefore, we couldn't change it anymore, we had no influence, I would say it would have deserved an intensified effort to get out of the report whatever is not in dispute, and if need be, replace it in a summary form whatever the parties agree on so the logic is not lost. I mean, it's not cutting out a whole part of an expert report, but to say well, on this and this matter, the parties do agree that this and this and they reach that agreement on the basis of A, B, C, series of documents which they will not now further explore but that is where the parties stand. That aspect, and that was the main comment I gave, Mr. Petrovic, that aspect has not been addressed satisfactorily as far as I'm concerned, but I'll further discuss it with my colleagues. And the Chamber would like to be informed very quickly about the underlying documents. I mean, if that takes translation effort until May 2013, then we might have a problem. Therefore, I'm more interested in your work-plan than an explanation on why things are as they are apparently at this moment. Ms. Marcus, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just to add to what has been said. We sent an e-mail, as I think my colleague Mr. Petrovic was referring to, on the 17th of November, which Your Honours have seen of course and which relates directly to what we are discussing here. We are, unfortunately and regrettably, not able to process the reports in B/C/S, and we wouldn't even if they were in English, we wouldn't be able to process them without the underlying documents, as well as a cross-referencing of the underlying documents, whether they are on the 65 ter list or not, et cetera, so that we can read the report which is based on underlying documents. So we would appreciate a specific idea of when we might be provided with the underlying documents in addition to the -- we have the approximate dead-lines of when we'll receive the English translations, we'd also like to know exactly when we can expect the underlying documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Petrovic, I mainly addressed what is in dispute and what is not in dispute. Of course, another matter is relevance. Now, perhaps it would be worthwhile to go through the report again and also to find out what really is needed or not. Of course, if we have a paragraph on -- paragraph on the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia armed forces and get an explanation of what the definition, the purpose, and the tasks of a land army are or of the navy, I take it that the navy will focus on what happens on the waters rather than on land, but of course, I've got no idea what to expect there, but it may be very important also to find out what we really need for this case, what the relevance is. Some portions of the document are very long. But, again, not having seen the report, not having seen the appendages, the appendages alone are well over 100 pages. I don't know what they are apart from that it's appendages to part 1, part 2, part 3 or part 4. But I really need a story different from the winter will be dark and long and there may fall snow. That's not the basis on which we can proceed. So, therefore, I would suggest that you present a work-plan including meeting with the Prosecution, seeing how -- you understand what I mean? It's the -- we want this part of your Defence case not to end up in a disastrous situation. I'll further discuss with my colleagues what we exactly understand by a work-plan because I'm using these words rather loosely at this moment and we might set a dead-line for that so that we are informed soon and that we do not -- it's like financial crisis or Euro crisis, Mr. Petrovic, the longer you wait, the more problematic the situation may become. We'll discuss it and you'll hear further instructions from the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC

utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. Thank you, this is just because of the transcript, a couple of the corrections are for the transcript to make sure that it's correct. The latter two, that is D384 and D385 under seal. And, Madam Registrar, you are instructed to make any changes to the extent necessary in this respect in e-court. Is that sufficiently clear?

utterances.text: Thank you. Then we'll now take a break first. Also in order to avoid that we all start suffering from a bookkeeper's syndrome, we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I first want to further address the status of parts of Witness Bosnic's testimony. The Prosecution has requested to lift the confidentiality. utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, dead-lines for your bar table motions. Numbers 1 and 2, 15th of December. Number 3 at the end of the winter recess. Which would mean, I think it's the 9th of January or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Petrovic, the Chamber will further consider what we exactly understand to be a work-plan for you in relation to the expert report and what we would expect you to -- and when you would be expected to submit to the Chamber how you intend to proceed, and again, very much on the practical level, the Chamber wants to avoid that we end up in major trouble as far as timing is concerned. We'll give you further instructions for that. Then I move on to the list of exhibits of which the status is to be considered. P2448.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, from our view there is no problem with any of the three Prosecution exhibits being made public. Thank you for the extra time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, public is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No concerns --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Ms. Marcus remains silent on the matter but agrees. D232 is a public exhibit from now on. I'd like to move on. I'm at this moment more or less addressing the public that -- and inform them that on the 7th of October, 2011, and the 11th of November, the Chamber has issued two confidential decisions granting in part applications from the Republic of Serbia for protective measures specifying the kind of material that is to be protected for national security interests for documents provided to the Prosecution and for the testimony of two Prosecution witnesses. Now, connected to this the -- pursuant to the 7th of October decision, the Prosecution filed on the 11th of November, 2011, a list of names of persons mentioned in those documents whose identities the Chamber has decided to protect. As the Chamber has noted in its decision, it is not readily apparent from the parties' submissions which of the Prosecution documents subject to this decision are in evidence before the Chamber. The Chamber, therefore, requests the Prosecution to file by the 15th of December, 2011, a list of the exhibits which are subject to the Chamber's decision of the 7th of October, 2011. Should documents subject to the decision be admitted at a later stage, the Prosecution is instructed to file a supplement to the list as soon as possible. I just wanted to verify whether this is clear for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Clear, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then -- then I would like to put on the record that the Prosecution's oral motion to compel disclosure of interview notes for Witness Novakovic, a motion of the 5th of October, 2011, was denied on the same day, and that the parties were informed through an informal communication. As for the reasons for this decision, I refer the parties to the Chamber's general reasons on this issue contained in the Chamber's 12th of October, 2011 decision on Prosecution urgent motion related to non-compliance of Stanisic Defence with Rule 65 ter G and Rule 67 of the rules. The next matter I would like to raise is the statement that was admitted in relation to Witness Dragicevic. The statement was admitted but the chart with comments and underlying documents were MFI'd. I, therefore, instruct the Stanisic Defence to communicate with the Registry and the Registry to file after that an internal memorandum with numbers assigned to any outstanding documents. Is that clear both to the Stanisic Defence and the Registry?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to hear further Defence submissions on the bar tabling of two suspect interview excerpts, excerpts that were tendered by the Prosecution after the testimony of Witness Helgers and would like to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it those submissions are substantial in the discussion, not merely practical, which doesn't even need to be put on the record, not to be referred to in more general terms on the record which we often do. Let me just consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The only problem we have with the Prosecution's suggestion is that those submissions contain submissions which go beyond the admissibility argument and goes to arguments about whether Mr. Stanisic should be accorded any mitigation for his actions in releasing the hostages and we would object to those submissions forming part of the trial record at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Perhaps this issue -- I'm perfectly glad to sit down with Mr. Jordash and have a discussion about it, how to proceed. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, of course, the first matter to be decided is whether they should be admitted, yes or no. Therefore, I invite you to sit together with Mr. Jordash and see whether you can make a distinction between the question which is before the Chamber at this very moment, that is admission. So, therefore, it might not be always easy to make a clear distinction between admission and matters apparently raised by the Prosecution. I have not read it until now, which perhaps is a good thing, I'll check with my colleagues whether they have read it -- yes, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: On reflection, I withdraw the objection to those submissions being filed. We'll file a written response, though, if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine because the Chamber decided that they should be filed, so whatever you have sent in your e-mail, you know, if it's of really substance, then it should be filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll receive a response by the Defence and if Mr. Petrovic want to respond as well, that's also, but a time-limit for that. Any suggestion, Mr. Jordash? Preferably this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: End of next week. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, then if we are going to respond too, we'll do so in writing.

utterances.text: Yes. I only set a dead-line now for the Stanisic Defence to file any submissions in response to the Prosecution e-mail submissions still to be filed by Friday the 2nd of December.
