Mr. Jordash, so, therefore, we'll give it a follow-up, but now not just we stick to the translation but whatever additional information can provide on why they did not change it and perhaps what they have considered, so a full explanation of the decision CLSS has taken and of course we'll then also find out whether it still takes that position yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We were going to file a brief response to that motion. I don't know if the dead-line would be the 29th, we can certainly expedite that. I wonder whether maybe that could be filed before the Registry's submission follows or as Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the Registry would wait until after you have filed a response, that might save a further round of exchange of views.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Madam Registrar, the Registry is urged not to file the 33(B) submission before the Prosecution has filed its response so the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps be a bit clearer on the submission by the Registry. CLSS -- the Registry is invited to inform the Chamber whether it maintains its position, I think that's already what I hinted at, and if so, for what reasons, also addressing the Stanisic Defence's arguments for a different translation. Yes. I'm addressing now the Simatovic Defence and the Chamber would like to have a list filed assigning provisional pseudonyms to each of your witnesses on your list, and that list should be filed before the first witness appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. The Stanisic Defence has indicated in an informal communication that it would like to call two of its witnesses out of turn, that is during or after the Simatovic Defence case. On the 4th of November, the Chamber has encouraged the Stanisic Defence to make such applications without delay. However, such applications have not been received to date, and just to clarify, the Chamber mainly encouraged you to make such applications formally so as to give the other parties as opportunity to review whether the calling of these witnesses out of turn would cause them any prejudice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I introduced the matter on historical grounds, how it was, because DST-060 I do understand is part of an agreement now. I'll put that on the record in a second. Now, there are a few questions in relation to this scheduling of witnesses. First of all, the Chamber does understand that there's an agreement that Witness DST-060 will be called first next week and, therefore, will delay the start of the presentation of evidence by the Simatovic Defence. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What is slightly uncertain at the moment is how long he will take. My estimation -- we haven't had a estimation from the parties, but it may well be that that witness can finish in two days. I don't intend to be more than an hour with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then one day remains next week, Wednesday. Is the Simatovic Defence ready to then call its first witness who could possibly start then on that Wednesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in informal communication, I'd addressed the Chamber, you have certainly seen what our position on this issue are. At this moment if my reckoning is correct, we have six Stanisic Defence witnesses who will testify and have not done so yet. Out of the six, we have considered, in the case of two or three of them, things carefully and we want to be as co-operative as we can, but we agree that these two or three can testify during our case, or perhaps after our case, although this may be a bit of a problem for us. But those two or three witnesses, DST-060, DST-071, and Witness Milovanovic who are to testify yet, it is very hard, almost impossible for us to begin our case unless these people have testified before as Stanisic Defence witnesses because their testimony is related to what the other two or three witnesses may say. The structure of our case itself depends on what we expect these witnesses may say before the Trial Chamber here. That is why we kindly request that these two witnesses complete their testimony and then literally within two or three days we will provide our witness list without any further delay. But the testimony of our witnesses before at least this part of the Defence case of Mr. Stanisic is finished would be a huge problem for us, and we can provide further explanation in writing, if necessary. Our understanding is that DST-060 can come on Monday. There are indications that Witness Milovanovic may be able to testify the following week, and if that is so, as soon as that is done, we can bring our first witness on any day of the week. We just kindly ask for some fundamental order that the orders of the Trial Chamber and the rules be observed. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Jordash, do we well understand that Witness DST-081 has been dropped by the Stanisic Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, but we are very close to doing so. We are trying to conduct some last-minute attempts to obtain some formalities and I think we'll know the answer to that by Monday and be able to make a decision, I think, early next week. I think it's -- I'll be frank, it's likely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay the Chamber would like to be informed at shortest possible notice. Then, Mr. Petrovic, we have dealt with Witness DST-060, an agreement is there. We have dealt with Mr. Milovanovic. Now, about the two remaining witnesses out of turn, DST-061 and Mr. Brown -- no, Mr. Brown and DST-071. DST-071, we know your position. We have discussed that. DST-061 is, let me just see, one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, DST-061, Mr. Brown, these two, what is your position in relation to them specifically to be called out of turn?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, although we believe that this is a departure from the usual order of things, we kindly ask the Chamber to accommodate us only in what is important to us. DST-060 and Mr. Milovanovic. For the other two witnesses, we agree that they be heard at any time during our case or after our case, that means DST-061 and expert Brown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your position in every respect is clear, Mr. Petrovic. Of course, it depends on developments in the coming days when the Chamber expects you to present your first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And since there is a risk that we would not have -- that we would have neither Mr. Milovanovic or Witness DST-071, you should, as I always requested also from the Stanisic Defence, you should develop a plan B.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will do our best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just with respect to the Simatovic Defence witnesses, we would like to -- we've sent an e-mail to them, I don't think we've received a response about the documents for their witnesses. We have not received the documents yet for the first witness that they intend to tender through that witness, so we would like to make sure that we receive those well in advance of the witness coming. If there's a chance that the first witness starts next Wednesday, we would like to receive the documents, if possible, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, in case of plan B, plan B documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we will do that today. We will provide the documents by close of business today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we move into private session. One second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Just to follow-up on the last part of the discussion before we went into private session, I see at this moment that -- but I have not yet looked at the Prosecution, that there seem to be no objections against Mr. Brown and Witness DST-061 to be called after the beginning of the Simatovic case. Any problems as far as the Prosecution is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We don't object, Your Honour, as long as they can come as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then just to have it clear on the record that the Chamber accepts that at least -- I'm not pronouncing the Chamber's views on the others, but at least Mr. Brown and Witness DST-061 are called out of turn. Then I have to deliver the reasons for a decision before we go to the MFI list. Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber delivers its decision on the Stanisic Defence motion on the admission of transcripts and associated exhibits pursuant to Rule 92 bis. It was on the 27th of September of this year that the Stanisic Defence filed a motion to admit the transcripts of evidence and associated exhibits in lieu of viva voce testimony of four witnesses: DST-057, DST-068, DST-071, and DST-080, pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The Prosecution responded to the request in relation to the witnesses 57, 68 and 80 on the 11th of October, 2011, and in relation to Witness DST-071 separately on the 20th of October, 2011. This followed a corrigendum filing by the Stanisic Defence and a decision of the Chamber to grant the Prosecution until the 20th of October to respond to the motion in relation to Witness 71. The Prosecution opposed the motion to tender the written evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis and request that all witnesses be called for cross-examination. On the 3rd of November, 2011, in an informal communication, the Stanisic Defence dropped witnesses DST-068, DST-080, and DST-057 from its witness list, leaving only the written evidence relating to witness DST-071 to be considered by the Chamber. On the 15th of November, 2011, the Chamber informed the parties that the Rule 92 bis motion dealing with Witness DST-071 was denied, and that the witness should be called for cross-examination. The Chamber now provides reasons for this decision. The Prosecution argued that Witness DST-071 must appear for cross-examination so as to clarify and give context to issues relating to the JNA and Serbian DB's role in arming, financing, and providing logistical support to military, TO, and volunteer groups, and to determine the witness's knowledge, if any, regarding the role of the Serbian DB members and the relation between the Serbian DB and the Red Berets. The Chamber considered that the witness's evidence relates to live and important issues between the parties. The Chamber, therefore, considered that the witness should be called for cross-examination and denied the Stanisic Defence request for admission of his written evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. We now move to the MFI list, the most exciting part of housekeeping sessions. And we'll start with Prosecution exhibits. We start with P2979. The Prosecution has not sought to tender the document on the 23rd of June, 2011, and it wanted it to have the document be MFI'd and possibly tender it at a later stage. At the same time, I note that the Stanisic Defence has questioned Witness DST-051 and Witness DST-032 about the document. Now, it has not been tendered. Could I receive an update from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do seek to tender it and exactly for the reasons that Your Honours has just mentioned. Since it's been used by both parties, we believe that Defence may not object to that, but we do seek to tender it at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm just trying to get on top of this issue. Our objection is -- we do have an objection. We have an objection that the document is admitted for the truth of its contents; we do not object to it being admitted for impeachment purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll further consider that and I'll refrain from a decision on the matter at this very moment. We move on, P2980, incomplete translation. Is there a full translation available?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's been uploaded at 0609-4870-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was nothing else which was an obstacle to admission, if I'm not mistaken. It's a document under seal. Madam Registrar, the full translation may replace the incomplete translation. P2980 is admitted under seal. Move on to P2984. It was originally admitted as an excerpt. Parties then agreed to have the entire document tendered. The full translation was not there yet. Is it now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's uploaded as 65 ter 6208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the uploaded full translation may replace the incomplete previous one. P2984 is admitted under seal. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I just wanted to make sure that our position on this is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought it was that, that the parties had agreed that -- on the entire document to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But only in light of my initial objection to the -- a portion of it being used, and once the portion had been admitted, we agreed to allow the rest of the file to be admitted because of the preliminary ruling. So we object for the reasons well known to the Chamber concerning the admission of this personnel file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say that -- but that was more or less rejected by our decision, and you say under those circumstances, then the whole of the -- then the entire document, but you are still not happy with the document to be admitted at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Full or in part. That's clear. It doesn't change the decision. It's now the full -- the full document together with the full translation that is admitted into evidence. Next one, P2986, stills from a video. The Stanisic Defence objected to admission until the relevance of this evidence was clear to it. The Prosecution then indicated that the relevance would be clear after the next piece of evidence was shown to the witness. However, neither party ever revisited this matter. Therefore, I'd like to receive an update whether the Stanisic Defence still objects to admission, or is convinced by the next piece of evidence that it is relevant evidence, and if relevant, whether there are any other objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. And I don't think that the Simatovic Defence objected to it. P2986 is admitted into evidence. Next one is P2988. It is a document listing names of a commission. Now, there is a similar, although not exactly the same list in P421. It seems that no party has objected to the document but that we just had not admitted it. Is that correctly understood, that there are no objections? No objections. P2988 is admitted under seal. I move on to P2989 which is objected to by the Stanisic Defence as it considers it to be an attempt by the Prosecution to covertly expound the Prosecution case, that's a matter that we dealt with in the guidance. Therefore, also in view of that decision, the prejudice is not sufficiently demonstrated and P2989 is admitted into evidence. For P2992, the same is true, same type of objection. Here also the prejudice is not sufficiently demonstrated, and P2992 is admitted into evidence. For P2995, excerpts from personnel files, the objections against admission were not the same for the two Defences. The Simatovic Defence was concerned about a lack of evidence of who owned the booklet contained in it and the lack of certification and the absence of stamps. Whereas the Stanisic Defence objected for different reasons, the same as with the two previous documents, that is lack of notice. There was another matter which is whether or not the excerpt, the selection made by the Prosecution of this personnel file, it was only an excerpt, whether there is any additional agreement between the parties whether additional pages should be added to this excerpt in case the Chamber would decide to admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as we know, the entire personnel file for this individual was tendered by the Simatovic Defence as D456 which is MFI'd. We didn't object to the admission of the complete file. I wonder whether that probably renders the debate about the excerpt of that file moot. I would suggest if the Chamber agrees with my assessment, that what we might do in this case, and this will come up as Your Honours probably already noticed, this comes up many times where one party tendered an excerpt of a personnel file and then later on the entire file is being tendered. In such cases, I would like to request or suggest that when we vacate the Exhibit for the excerpt or that we either, I don't know how technically it would be done but we mark it not admitted with a surrogate sheet that enables someone to cross-reference because, of course, in the record we are discussing one exhibit number which later on becomes a part, an excerpt of a larger exhibit. Just to enable cross referencing we would recommend that as a technical solution but of course we leave it up to Your Honours to think about that aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, as far as D456 is concerned, there is a translation missing, so whether or not it is exactly the same, the Chamber has some difficulties in comparing this excerpt with D456, and there's another matter, there's also a redaction issue in relation to D456, where, of course, the -- it seems that this may have been resolved between the Simatovic Defence and the government of Serbia, at the same time as we indicated before, this does not in itself bind the other parties so we do not know whether the Prosecution nevertheless would insist on an unredacted copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I see, Your Honour, yes, I should have mentioned that we submitted the complete file for translation. As soon as that's ready it can be uploaded and attached. That's with regard to the translation. With respect to the redactions, I'll have to check that. We do object to unredacted documents being tendered. I would also like to confirm whether this file is probably part of our negotiations with the government of Serbia as to unredacted versions and Serbia has agreed to provide that for the ones that -- so I think that that will be forthcoming and we can provide that as soon as we get it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, at this moment it's too early to already decide on P2995, but we should clearly keep in mind that it's directly linked to D456 and all the problems related to that last document. Then we'll move on -- yes, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Just to secure the record, we don't agree with Ms. Marcus when she suggests that the issue is moot because the party -- a party then puts in an additional part of the record. We still object to the part of the personnel file and the full file for the reasons we've given earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have to check, as a matter of fact, whether you objected to D456. Perhaps not because there was no translation yet. We'll have a look at it. We'll leave it open for the time being. Then I move on to P2996. I think that was also a notice matter. The Stanisic Defence objected on the 14th of July. Notice of the Prosecution, what they are doing, why they are doing it, and why they are doing it so late, that's -- I could refer to it again as the guidance issue. Now, there was another problem, that the English translation of page 3 was missing. Could I first verify whether that translation is complete now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The complete translation has been uploaded as BG03-2792-ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then the new translation replaces the old incomplete one. And P2996 is admitted into evidence. The objection by the Stanisic Defence is overruled because the prejudice has not sufficiently been demonstrated. Then we move on to P2997. The first question I'd like to ask the Prosecution, whether apart from what else remains, whether this would be a document that should be under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's then one. Then there was a Simatovic Defence objection about date and lack of probative value. I think it's on the record that I pronounce that this goes rather to weight than to admissibility. Now, the Stanisic Defence objected again on a different ground, that is, lack of notice. But apart from that objection, the Stanisic Defence also wished to reserve its position because you had not been in a position to re-examine the witness given that the document came from a disclosure of 109 personnel files in B/C/S, which you had no time to review. Lack of notice is clear. The other reservation, Mr. Jordash, could you update the Chamber on whether now having had an opportunity to look at this disclosure, and not having had a possibility to re-examine the witness, whether you still wish now -- knowing the content, whether you still wish to re-examine the witness and that he should be recalled for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the issue of notice is what is at the foundation of that objection, that had we had, first of all, notice that the file would be used, we would have approached a significant part of our case differently, and in any event now the file has been used, we still do not know what the Prosecution say that man did, what his acts and conducts were and what the legal categorisation of them are. So we are in the same position. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said at the time that you had no opportunity to re-examine the witness because you had no time -- you had had no time to review the material. Now, you have had that time and apart from all the other problems that may remain, does that trigger a wish to recall the witness to be re-examined on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, for the reasons that I've just outlined, that I don't know the significance of that person within the Prosecution case so I wouldn't know how to re-examine the witness on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So, therefore, there's no such request. Then the Simatovic Defence objection is denied due to weight rather than admissibility. The -- what remains of the Stanisic Defence objections, prejudice has not sufficiently been -- has not been demonstrated sufficiently and, therefore, that objection is denied. P2997 is admitted into evidence under seal. We move on to P3008. The Prosecution has sought only to tender a few pages of this personnel file. Had, however, uploaded the entire document. The Stanisic Defence has objected that the Prosecution had not met the Prlic appeal threshold. The Simatovic Defence agreed with that and also didn't think that it was appropriate for the Prosecution to tender through this witness. That is, again, if I could say so, the guidance issue. Now, what I'm wondering is whether the Prosecution would be willing to reduce the documents to the pages shown to the witness plus whatever any other party would want to have added to that for purposes of contextualisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have done that already. We've reduced the document according to what we understood to be the instructions of the Chamber on this issue. We have reduced it and uploaded it to 65 ter 6240.1. We are also, of course, happy to accept any additional portions of the file that the Defence wishes to add to that, but we have at this point only included the excerpts that were discussed with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any wish, apart from the objections against admission, that if it would be admitted, that for further contextualisation other parts of the document or, should I say the personnel file, should be added?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have some time to check that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Petrovic, same time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Middle of next week, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Middle of next week. I then set the dead-line at the 1st of December. Now, may I take it that since P3009 addresses exactly the same problems, that you would need that time for P3009 as well? Also another personnel file. Has it been reduced, Ms. Marcus, that one?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and it's uploaded as 65 ter 6241.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the Chamber would decide to admit, would any of the Defence teams want to add pages for contextualisation? Also 1st of December, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's then true both for you and Mr. Petrovic. I'm looking at the clock, I think it would be good to have a break. I meanwhile received confirmation that it is possible to have a hearing this afternoon. Now, at what time would we start. I have a meeting at 2.00. I suggest quarter past 3.00. Would that be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll now take a break and we resume at a quarter to 1.00 and since it's very unlikely that we would finish this morning, we'll continue this afternoon at quarter past 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we were at P3023. Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please accept my apologies for interrupting you, but I would like your permission to say just a few words regarding the continuation of the trial and the bringing of witnesses. Your Honours, I'm now talking about the plan B that you ordered me to prepare. If the Trial Chamber should not grant our request that Milovanovic testify before the beginning of our case, and if Milovanovic is unable to appear on Wednesday or the week of 5th December, I kindly ask the Trial Chamber that our plan B come into effect as of the 5th of December to avoid all uncertainty, first of all, as to what we are supposed to tell our witnesses concerning organisation, procedure, et cetera. So basically, if our two requests are rejected, that the plan B starts as of the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider it, Mr. Petrovic. I must say that many things have changed over the last 30 minutes, one of them I'd like to briefly discuss in private session. Could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I think we are at P3023. That is the, if I could say so, the Milosevic document. The Stanisic Defence has accepted admission for impeachment purposes but opposed for the truth of the content. The Simatovic Defence also opposed admission. The Chamber admits P3023 and not explicitly or exclusively for impeachment purposes, which, by the way, does not mean that the Chamber would easily, on the basis of this document alone, accept the, if I could say so, the truth of what Mr. Milosevic submitted in that document and we'll carefully consider what weight to be given to the document in the context of the evidence in its entirety. Then I move on to P3025 up to and including P3028, four 1992 reports concerning White Eagles. Objections were there based on redactions. The Prosecution submitted that it would be happy to tender the unredacted documents but it just doesn't have them and that it would request unredacted copies, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have those unredacted copies. For P3025, the unredacted version has been uploaded as 65 ter 6263.1. And for P3026, the unredacted version has been uploaded as 65 ter 6264.1. For P3027, the unredacted version is uploaded as 65 ter 6265.1. And for P3028, the unredacted version is uploaded as 65 ter 6266.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. The objection was based on redactions. Simatovic Defence, are there any further objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that P3025, up to and including P3028 are admitted into evidence. Now, Ms. Marcus, since they are now unredacted copies, is there any need to have them under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then they are admitted as public documents. Next one P3029, the Stanisic Defence sought an opportunity to inspect the content and the parties would further discuss whether anything else would be needed for contextualisation, and I'd like to have an update. Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't remember this issue in that way. I'm just looking at the Prosecution's chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you take your time to look at it and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think these were uploaded only last night, I think, and that's why we haven't been able to turn our minds to it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were uploaded last night? Or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm double-checking, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile, I abuse the time available to instruct the Registry and this deals with the previous documents, to have the new unredacted copies -- to have the old redacted copies be replaced by the numbers mentioned before by Ms. Marcus, and I'm talking about P3025 up to and including P3028. Ms. Marcus, uploaded when?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have that information yet, my Case Manager is looking for it. But if I could add on the issue of P3029.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly one more issue on this. We made an application on the 7th of October, 2011, I had like to renew that application to admit other portions of this file. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll hear from the Defence whether there are any further submissions. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I can't remember the reasons why the Prosecution say they should be added so perhaps if we could hear what the reasons are. I mean, I would in any event need to see the additions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that you deal with it -- that you explain each other's position out of court, that we'll then hear what then remains as objections. Then I move on to P3032. The issue being that the OTP did not -- there are two statements. They were not tendered and there seems to be an agreement that only smaller portions of the statement would be uploaded. Further, the source of the statements was unclear. Could I hear whether smaller portions of the document have been uploaded and whether there is further information as to the source of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the smaller portion has been uploaded as 65 ter 6277.1. As to the origin, I'm sorry, I didn't have that noted down, but I will check that and get back to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll not decide on admission at this moment. I then move to the last Prosecution exhibit, P3033. B/C/S translation was missing. Is it there now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. It is uploaded as 65 ter 6276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Madam Registrar, would you please attach that to the Exhibit P3033. Were there any objections against it? I have not any notes of objections. If not, P3033, report of the Humanitarian Law Fund, is admitted into evidence. We move to the -- to the Defence exhibits. For D129, it may be better to put that on hold waiting for the new bar table submissions because they most likely would include or possibly would include this document, D129. utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would then be D129, D130, and D150. Now, for D159, I would say a similar matter applies, that they may appear on the bar table submission. At the same time here is an additional issue of redactions. Of course, we do not know whether this will be resolved in your, if I could call them like that, your 54 bis discussions with the -- with the Serbian government, that's one, but if not, then, of course, the Chamber would have to know what kind of redactions are made before we can make any determination whether it's acceptable to have it admitted. So, therefore, if still redacted, I think it would be good to have it clearly stated in the bar table submissions what the redactions are about. Then I move on to a series of documents which is D230 up to and including D251. There's one in those series which might need specific attention, but I first go to what is common to all of these. The Prosecution had objected to the admission of the associated exhibits because it's -- these are associated exhibits to a -- to a witness statement, a 92 ter statement, until it had some understanding of where and how these documents were covered in the statement. Therefore, for all these documents the Chamber would like to know whether there are still any authenticity or provenance concerns.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We do not object to the admission through the bar table, we'd submit, of D230, D231 and D235. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is D232.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say English translation incomplete.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, otherwise on D232 we do not object to its admission provided we can have information about origin. So that document has the two issues, the translation and the provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: With respect to D237 MFI, the document was not contained in the witness comments chart nor included in the notice documents for use with DST-051 to the best of our knowledge and we seek further information as to its provenance. And for D248, we seek only information about its origin, same goes for D249, D250, and D251.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that D246 is ready to be admitted, and is hereby admitted. Now, for D245, Ms. Marcus, I'm asking you to assist me because since you didn't took the normal order, D245 is? Was that the one that was not dealt with? Or ... Let me just check because I lost track for a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I have that in a separate entry. Yes, we do have a position on that. We maintain our objection providing -- regarding authenticity until we receive information about its origin. That's for D245.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And then D242 is ready to be admitted, if I understand you well. Objections dropped.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D242 is admitted into evidence. Then D237, Mr. Jordash, nowhere traced in the witness statement and apart from that another problem, do you insist on -- then perhaps you explain to Ms. Marcus, not necessarily at this very moment, why is it nevertheless in the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, we've -- I think the outstanding objection to that was that it was -- they needed further information as to provenance, but we've provided it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think it was -- I think it was -- let me see with respect to D237 MFI, the document was not contained in the witness comments chart, not included in the notice document for use with DST-051 to the best of the knowledge of the Prosecution, and we seek further information as to its provenance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, in relation to the first part, it's unclear whether the Prosecution object to relevance and probative value. We accept that the -- we accept the assertion that it wasn't connected to the chart or witness, but we'd submit it pursuant to the bar table procedure. We've indicated to the Prosecution that -- we've indicated on two occasions that it was received from the National Council and the RFA was 1D4884. Indicates on the 29th of June, and then the 3rd of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, we drop our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that D237 is admitted into evidence. What we then have the objections against D235 are still there, Ms. Marcus, if I'm -- D232, English translation incomplete. utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'll accept Mr. Jordash's assertion on that.

utterances.text: Did you have any other --

utterances.text: Yes, we wanted information about the origin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any information about the origin, Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS

utterances.text: D232 is admitted into evidence. I think only two now of the series are still missing. Let me just ... Yes, there were no objections against D230 and D231. Therefore, D230 is admitted into evidence, D231 is admitted into evidence. I think we had this series now complete.

utterances.text: Yes, it was not complete yet. Objections against D235 were -- are not there anymore, therefore, also D235 is admitted into evidence. Then we come to D253. utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it has not been resolved yet. It could be our mistake but it also could be some confusion. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Your Honour, we sent the translation to the Simatovic Defence on the 9th of September. It is ERN 0606-0093 up to and including 0606-0110. We can find that e-mail and resend it if it seems to have fallen through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the other matter was that you would have a look at the pages 1 to 8, whether it was of any concern to you that we start only at fax page number 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like another moment to check that. I didn't have that aspect noted down. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then next item D266, translation was pending. Is the translation there now?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that document does not relate to our Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that -- yes, no, it has been dealt with already in the housekeeping session we earlier dealt with it. utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. D266 is admitted into evidence. D271 -- D271 is the chart with the witness's comment on documents to be ten dared as evidence with that witness, Witness DST-035. utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Our concern is precisely as Your Honour has outlined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And has the Defence looked at it? I mean, if the parties agree that it's a typo, that may well be clear from the document itself, then the matter is resolved, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, we would just request then that a corrigendum cover sheet be uploaded so that it can be attached to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we just return to that in two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The objection is withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is withdrawn. D272 is admitted into evidence. utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D274 is admitted into evidence. D276. Prosecution objected to the irrelevance of this partial translation of a newspaper article. Could the Stanisic Defence further explain the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we drop our objection as to relevance. Sorry to interrupt, but we would maintain our objection until the full translation of the article is provided, that was the other aspect of the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And is there a B/C/S original because I think it was not there? So you withdraw the objection but you are waiting for the full translation, and then I have a note here that a B/C/S original wasn't available.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: B/C/S original is uploaded and we are just waiting for the translation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll leave it at that at this moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to D271 -- sorry, yes, D271, the Prosecution and the assertion that the witness commented 1D37 instead of 1D377, the confusion arose because the B/C/S version was under 1D37 and the English version was under 1D377.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and how are we going to fix this then? Because we have now established what the confusion was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we just select one, 1D377, and label both in that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Maybe I'm not understanding. If our understanding as it is that the witness commented on 1D377, so are you saying - sorry - that the English version of 1D37 was uploaded as 1D377? Because it's obviously the underlying document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, it was mislabelled in the chart. That was my confusion. In the chart that we put forward 1D377 was the English one and the B/C/S 1D37 and it would make sense since the witness commented on 1D377 that that remains the number for both.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. So it seems we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it seems you do. Let me see where I was. I think we were at D277. The Prosecution wanted additional information as to the provenance of the document, and also who made the decisions about what portions would be shown to the Chamber and what criteria were used and how it can be assured that it was done accurately. Could we hear from the Stanisic, is one of the famous reports with redactions we discussed earlier this week or the excerpts, I should say excerpts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Precisely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that is a matter still to be discussed, I take it, with the Serbian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we leave that open for the time being, Ms. Marcus. Any further comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We also sought information as to provenance, which we can receive when we receive the other information as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it it comes from the Serbian government, otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll leave that open. I move to D279 up to and including D290. Translations were not there. The translations have now been uploaded and attached. The Prosecution has informed the Chamber that no more objections against admission do exist in relation to D280 up to and including D290. In this series, I also have D279, Ms. Marcus, any objections against D279.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'd like information on provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, can you answer? These are all commission documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If it's a commission document, I'm assured -- I'll relatively sure and I'll have it confirmed that Mr. Stanisic received them from the head of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, to the best of our information this is not a commission document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I made a mistake because I referred to them as commission documents. Could you perhaps I could have a look at it, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we are going to need a bit more time to find out the provenance, I am afraid. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then D280 up to and including D290 are admitted into evidence. And D279 is still MFI'd. The next one, D291, State Security Service 3rd department Official Note. I think redactions was the problem. Most likely subject to your conversations at this moment, Mr. Jordash, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that remains MFI'd awaiting the outcome of your conversations with the Serbian government. Then D292, translation was faulty, there was a revised translation. Has the revised translation been uploaded?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it may be attached to the -- to D292 and D292 since there were no objections as far as I know, but Ms. Marcus, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are no objections. We just would suggest that the document remain under seal and that the Simatovic Defence needs to inform Serbia that the document was used so that they can have an opportunity to seek protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D292 is admitted under seal, at least provisionally. D293, the Prosecution would like to see the request for assistance from the Stanisic Defence in relation to this document. Does your objection stand, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that you have had no access to the RFA or has the access to the RFA raised any further concerns?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To my -- to the best of my knowledge we have not received the RFA, but I have to say that if we can be informed of which RFA it was received, that may be sufficient for us to drop our objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is for the Simatovic team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Mr. Petrovic, under what RFA was this document received?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to put the ball back into the court of my colleague Mr. Jordash. The document is 1D2460. It's from the 65 ter list of the Stanisic Defence and we used it from that list, so I don't believe I can answer the question of the provenance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: If we could have some time for that check, too. We think it came from the National Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we leave it to that for the time being. As I said before, there are some uncertainties about this afternoon. I would -- I would like -- the parties to remain standby so that the Chamber has two or three minutes to further consider how we will proceed. We'll, therefore, take a very short break. --- Break taken at 1.41 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I said before, it was uncertain whether we could proceed this afternoon. Due to unforeseen circumstances, unforeseen circumstances being circumstances not foreseen one hour ago, I should say perhaps one hour and a half ago when I announced the be possibility of sitting this afternoon, there are no three judges who are available and fit to be in this afternoon session and that's the reason why we have to cancel that option. Now, that means that because we want to finish this housekeeping session, that we change slightly also the next week schedule. We'll start on Monday finishing this housekeeping session which takes most likely anything between one hour and a half or close to two hours. I do not know whether it's of any use to even apply for the possibility that the accused will arrive a bit later because they are not very much interested, which I fully understand, in this housekeeping session, but we'll start somewhere in the afternoon of Wednesday -- of Monday afternoon the hearing of the witness, DST-060. That will then be continued and on the base of a schedule that might be possible to finish that witness in two days, would that include cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, we are waiting for the Prosecution and the Simatovic team to give an estimation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry, we stand by our estimate of approximately four hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, up to 45 minutes is our estimate and we'll be trying to reduce it even further if it fits into the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, what was the time, I apologise for not having the original estimate in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not sure I have it in mind, but I estimate I'll be about an hour with the witness and in that vein I would simply remind the Chamber of the usual examination to cross-examination distribution of, I think it's 170 per cent for the cross-examining party.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence original estimate for that witness before he was converted to 92 ter was four hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, that would make four hours to four hours, that's a hundred per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, but this is now 92 ter, so I'm just relying upon what we were asked to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I look at the whole of it, we would have one -- up to one-half session on Monday which is effectively a little bit less than two hours, we would have three effective hours on Tuesday and we would have three effective hours on Wednesday which should be enough to conclude the evidence of the witnesses. I would like to invite the parties to make a strict schedule so that they reconsider again whether they really need all the time and that the Chamber is being guided by the parties as when to stop, and it's usually efficiency of examination-in-chief, and cross-examination is a matter of being fully prepared and being fully focused. I already add to this that on Wednesday there will be only two judges. We'll sit 15 bis, I'll not be available on Wednesday. Then we adjourn for the day and we'll resume on Monday, the 28th of November, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in this same Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
